title: Any-to-Any: Building Native Multimodal Agents - Patrick Löber, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A Gemini API developer walks through building a NotebookLM-style agent that ingests PDFs/audio/video, then uses a reasoning model with function calling to invoke specialized image and speech generation models in a loop. Most content is Gemini product marketing, but a few concrete API mechanics (context caching, token budgets, file/URL inputs, skill-style tool declarations) are copyable.

takeaways.technique: Context caching for repeated queries over large inputs
takeaways.what_they_do: Upload long files once via the File API and enable built-in context caching so repeated queries against the same content reuse the cached prefix instead of re-billing full input tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can combine it with context caching... especially useful if you're loading longer files into Gemini and doing repeated queries because then it saves you 90% of the costs
takeaways.numbers: ~90% cost savings on repeated queries over long files

takeaways.technique: Modality token budgeting and time-window slicing
takeaways.what_they_do: They give concrete token-per-minute ratios for audio/video and show that you can restrict analysis to timestamp ranges instead of ingesting whole files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 1 minute of audio translates to a 1920 tokens... you can tell it to look at only different timestamps. So, for example, only analyze from minute 5 to minute 15
takeaways.numbers: 1 min audio ≈ 1920 tokens; 1M token limit ≈ 9+ hours audio or ~1 hour video

takeaways.technique: Ship API usage as an agent skill instead of memorized code
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than teaching agents the SDK by heart, they package the API usage patterns as a 'skill' the agent can load when it needs to call the models.

takeaways.technique: Reasoning model + specialized generator tools in a loop
takeaways.what_they_do: A reasoning model decides what artifacts are needed and calls specialized single-purpose models via function declarations, looping until assets are sufficient, rather than a hardcoded pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent should be able to decide what to create rather than where we hard code the pipeline... it acts in a loop and reasons if we need more assets or if it's good enough

takeaways.technique: Cheap small models for transcription/extraction subtasks
takeaways.what_they_do: They note even the smallest flash models transcribe audio well when simply prompted to produce a transcript, so heavy reasoning models aren't needed for extraction.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Flash and even the smallest ones, Flashlight, is pretty good at transcribing audio. If you just tell it in the prompt generate a transcript of this file
